title: Year 10 mock: 4MA1-style Higher Paper 1 and Paper 2 (calculator)
subject: Mathematics
source: Written for mathematics/y10 lessons 114, 115, 116, 117 (Year 10 mock: original 4MA1-style Higher papers (Paper 1 and Paper 2, calculator) with mark scheme (portal quiz, secure mode, and printable paper))
intro: Lessons 114 to 117. Own 4MA1-style questions written for TGA, in four 35-minute parts. Show every method; about a minute a mark.

questions.q: Write 0.4̇5̇ (0.454545...) as a fraction in its simplest form. [2]
Write 360 as a product of prime factors, then find the HCF of 360 and 84. [3]
£4,000 is invested for 5 years at 3% per year compound interest: find its value. [3]
After a 15% reduction a price is £221: find the original price. [3]
Factorise 6x² + 7x - 3 and hence solve 6x² + 7x - 3 = 0. [4]
A histogram class 10 ≤ t < 25 has frequency 30: find its frequency density; the class 25 ≤ t < 30 has frequency density 4.8: find its frequency. [4]
A sector has radius 9 cm and angle 80°: find its arc length and perimeter to 3 sf. [4]
A car travels 145 km in 1 hour 40 minutes: find its average speed in km/h. [3]
Work out (6.4 × 10⁵) ÷ (1.6 × 10⁻²) in standard form; a metal has density 2.7 g/cm³: find the mass of 1.5 × 10³ cm³ of it. [4]
Find the equation of the line through (2, -1) and (6, 11). [3]
Find the equation of the line perpendicular to y = 2x + 5 through (4, 1). [3]
Solve x² - 6x + 4 = 0, giving your answers to 2 dp. [4]
Solve x² - x - 12 < 0. [3]
An arithmetic sequence has first term 7 and common difference 4: find the nth term and the sum of the first 20 terms. [4]
Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 156°: find the number of sides and the sum of the interior angles. [4]
Simplify fully (x² - 9)/(x² + 5x + 6). [4]
(a) Make s the subject of v² = u² + 2as (b) Make x the subject of y = (3x + 2)/(x - 1). [5]
Share £540 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. [3]
Simplify √50 + √18. [2]
Find the value of 27^(2/3) and of 16^(-1/2). [3]
Times (minutes): 0 < t ≤ 10 (4), 10 < t ≤ 20 (11), 20 < t ≤ 30 (15), 30 < t ≤ 40 (10): write the modal class and estimate the mean. [4]
y is directly proportional to x²; y = 50 when x = 5: find y when x = 7. [3]
Solve 3x + 2y = 16 and 5x - 2y = 8. [4]
AB = AC and angle BAC = 40°; BC is extended to D: find angle ACD, giving reasons. [4]
questions.a: angle ACB = 70° (base angles of an isosceles triangle) (M1 B1); angle ACD = 110° (angles on a straight line) (A1 B1).

questions.q: B is 8 km due east of A and C is 6 km due north of B: find the distance AC and the bearing of A from B. [4]
questions.a: √(64 + 36) (M1) = 10 km (A1); bearing of A from B = 270° (B2).

questions.q: A sector of radius 7.5 cm has area 30 cm²: find its angle to 1 dp. [4]
A car worth £18,000 depreciates by 12% a year: find its value after 3 years. [3]
Expand and simplify (2x - 3)(x + 4)(x - 1). [3]
Write x² - 4x - 1 in the form (x + a)² + b; hence give the turning point of y = x² - 4x - 1 and solve x² - 4x - 1 = 0 exactly. [4]
A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 8 s, then travels at 20 m/s for 12 s: find its acceleration and the total distance. [4]
A population rises by 4% one year and falls by 4% the next: find the overall percentage change. [3]
A force of 600 N acts on an area of 0.25 m²: find the pressure; convert a density of 2.7 g/cm³ to kg/m³. [4]
Prove that (2n + 1)² - (2n - 1)² is a multiple of 8 for every integer n. [4]
Construct the perpendicular bisector of a 9 cm line AB (photograph and upload). [2]
questions.a: arcs shown; bisector meets AB at 4.5 cm at 90° (B2).

questions.q: A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a semicircle of diameter 8 cm removed from one end: find the area left, exact and to 3 sf. [4]
Boys and girls are in the ratio 5 : 4; 12 more boys join and the ratio becomes 3 : 2: how many pupils were there at first? [4]
Class A: median 54, IQR 12; class B: median 61, IQR 25: compare the marks. [2]
questions.a: B higher on average (median 61 > 54) (B1); A more consistent (IQR 12 < 25) (B1).

questions.q: A price rises by 20% and then by 10%: find the single percentage increase. [3]

blocks.note: Own questions in the 4MA1 style; check the format against Pearson's sample assessment materials.
